column3: With respect to the Hampton Towne Centre Mortgage Loan (2.9%), the borrower sponsor disclosed an ongoing dispute with the third largest tenant, Riverside Physician (“Riverside”), representing approximately 15.5% of the net rentable square footage, regarding Riverside’s claimed entitlement to a $636,250 tenant improvement allowance under its lease agreement (the “Riverside Lease”). At origination, the borrower deposited $318,125 (half the disputed amount) into an unfunded obligations reserve; the remaining $318,125 is recourse to the borrower and the guarantor. Pursuant to the Mortgage Loan documents, such recourse will terminate upon the occurrence of any one of the following, in each case with deliveries reasonably satisfactory to the lender: (i) evidence that Riverside is in occupancy and operating in its leased premises and paying full, unabated monthly rent and reimbursements (the “Riverside Lease Occupancy Evidence”) and an estoppel from Riverside confirming: (a) occupancy, operation, and payment of full rent and reimbursements; (b) no outstanding tenant improvement allowances, reimbursements, or credits, and no rights to offset, reduce, or avoid payment of rent or other charges; and (c) no existing defaults under the Riverside Lease; (ii) the Riverside Lease Occupancy Evidence, and a letter from Riverside to the borrower confirming there is no ongoing dispute as to any outstanding tenant improvement allowance and that Riverside has received all amounts to which it is entitled; or (iii) as of January 16, 2027, the Riverside Lease Occupancy Evidence and an affidavit from the borrower and the borrower sponsor and a search of court records in Delaware, Texas, and Virginia (including the city and county records where the mortgaged property is located) confirming that (a) no judicial or enforceable claims have been filed against the borrower by Riverside and (b) Riverside has not otherwise demanded payment of any tenant
